full_text_en:
Shandong Provincial Food Import and Export Company, Shandong Shanfu Group Co., Ltd., Shandong Shanfu Risui Co., Ltd. v. Ma Daqing, Qingdao Shengk Dacheng Trade Co., Ltd. — dispute over unfair competition

Ruling Summary

Under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the fact that an interest deserves protection does not alone constitute a sufficient condition for the injured party to obtain civil relief. Although a business opportunity constitutes a legal interest that may be protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, it is not itself a statutory right, and the conclusion of a transaction does not depend solely on the will of one party but requires the mutual agreement of both parties to the transaction. Therefore, others are free to compete for such transactional opportunities. Competition among competitors for business opportunities is the normal state of competition and is encouraged and promoted by market competition. With respect to the same business opportunity, when one competitor gains, another loses. For the injured party to obtain civil relief, it must also prove that the competitor's conduct was improper. Only when a competitor, in competing for business opportunities, fails to follow the principle of good faith, violates generally accepted commercial morality, and seizes by improper means a business opportunity that another party could reasonably expect to obtain, is such conduct prohibited by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

Commercial morality must be evaluated according to the ethical standards of market transaction participants—that is, economic persons—in a specific commercial field. It is neither the same as personal moral character nor equivalent to general social ethics; rather, it embodies a kind of commercial ethics. The commercial morality required by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law must be generally accepted commercial morality, referring to behavioral standards commonly recognized and accepted within a specific commercial field, and must be generally accepted and universal. Even within the same commercial field, because it involves moral norms in market transactions, generally accepted commercial morality should be a behavioral standard commonly and universally recognized by all transaction participants, and cannot be judged solely from the perspective of one side, such as the buyer or seller, the enterprise or its employee, in determining whether it constitutes generally accepted commercial morality. Specifically, in a particular case, generally accepted commercial morality should be determined by analyzing the specific commercial field and the circumstances of the case (such as general practices in the specific industry, consequences of the conduct, the subjective state of the parties to the transaction, and the voluntary choice of the counterparty, etc.).

As workers with learning ability, employees will inevitably master and accumulate knowledge, experience, and skills related to the work they perform during the course of their employment with the enterprise. Unless such knowledge, experience, and skills constitute trade secrets of the enterprise, they are part of the employee's personality and form the basis of their ability to survive and work. After resignation, an employee has the freedom to autonomously utilize their own knowledge, experience, and skills. If, by using such knowledge, experience, and skills, the employee wins the trust of clients and gains a competitive advantage, this does not violate the principle of good faith or generally accepted commercial morality, unless the former enterprise's trade secrets are infringed. Where there is neither a violation of a non-compete obligation nor an infringement of trade secrets, if a worker uses the knowledge, experience, and skills learned at the former employer to serve another entity that competes with the former employer, it should not be readily found to constitute unfair competition simply by applying the principle provision of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2009) Min Shen Zi No. 1065

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shandong Provincial Food Import and Export Company, domiciled at Floor 6, Shanfu Building, No. 96, Xianggang Zhong Lu, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Ma Daqing, male, born April 8, 1963, Han nationality, domiciled at Unit 2, Room 702, No. 38, Jiangxi Lu, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Agent ad litem: Guo Xinzhen, Attorney at Wenkang Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over unfair competition between Shandong Provincial Food Import and Export Company (hereinafter referred to as Shandong Food Company), Shandong Shanfu Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanfu Group Company), Shandong Shanfu Risui Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanfu Risui Company), on the one hand, and Qingdao Shengk Dacheng Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shengk Dacheng Company) and Ma Daqing, on the other, the Shandong High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2008) Lu Min San Zhong Zi No. 83 on March 18, 2009, which has become legally effective. On June 18, 2009, Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Risui Company filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to examine this case, and held a public hearing on October 14, 2009. Agents ad litem of Shandong Food Company and Shanfu Risui Company, Zou Weining and Chen Jing, Agent ad litem of Shanfu Group Company, Zou Weining and Ma Chunsheng, Agent ad litem of Shengk Dacheng Company, Zhang Jinhai, and Agent ad litem of Ma Daqing, Guo Xinzhen, attended the proceedings. This case is now concluded upon examination.

Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Risui Company jointly applied for retrial, alleging: The second-instance judgment misinterpreted the facts of this case, found facts subjectively and one-sidedly, and incorrectly applied the law. They requested that a retrial be initiated, that the civil judgment (2008) Lu Min San Zhong Zi No. 83 of the Shandong High People's Court be revoked, and that the civil judgment (2007) Qing Min San Chu Zi No. 136 of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court be upheld. Their reasons were as follows: 1. The second-instance judgment completely severed the internal connections among the facts of this case, finding facts in an isolated and one-sided manner. In this case, Ma Daqing subjectively harbored malice to seize the business opportunities of Shandong Food Company through improper means to obtain huge profits, and objectively implemented a series of planned, step-by-step, and premeditated unfair competition acts to seize the business opportunities of Shandong Food Company. In finding the facts, the second-instance judgment ignored the facts that the evidence materials in this case were sufficient to prove, severing the connections among facts. (1) The second-instance judgment one-sidedly examined the facts of the case, ignoring the main facts. The second-instance judgment held that when Ma Daqing represented Shengk Dacheng Company in seeking trading opportunities from China National Cereals, Oils, Foodstuffs Import & Export (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as COFCO), he had already left Shandong Food Company, and his contract with Shanfu Risui Company had expired and terminated; after leaving Shandong Food Company, Ma Daqing, in a proper manner, helped Shengk Dacheng Company obtain the trading opportunity; Shengk Dacheng Company's act of seeking the trading opportunity was merely submitting a request to COFCO to engage in the business of exporting Japanese kelp. However, a comprehensive review of the facts of the case shows that the unfair competition acts of Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company were a series of acts from mid-2006 or even earlier to after 2007, including Ma Daqing's planning and preparing to establish a new company (i.e., Shengk Dacheng Company) while still employed by the applicants for retrial, requesting Shandong Food Company to abandon the kelp patent, going to Japan in the name of Shengk Dacheng Company to lobby Japanese customers, soliciting the company's kelp business personnel to resign and work for him, spreading news to kelp farmers that he had obtained kelp quotas, as well as leaving his post without authorization and taking away most of the company's kelp business materials, among others. Ma Daqing had already completed the work of seizing kelp quotas during the period of his employment, and obtaining quotas through so-called inspection after his unauthorized resignation was merely a smokescreen. (2) The second-instance judgment severed the relationship between Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company, leading to unclear findings of fact. The second-instance judgment held that after leaving Shandong Food Company, Ma Daqing, in a proper manner, helped Shengk Dacheng Company obtain the trading opportunity, not violating principles such as good faith, and his behavior was not improper and constituted fair competition; Shengk Dacheng Company's act of seeking the trading opportunity was merely submitting a request to COFCO to engage in the business of exporting Japanese kelp. In fact, the relationship between Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company was not a so-called "helping" relationship, nor a relationship between a worker and the employing company; Shengk Dacheng Company's act of seeking the trading opportunity was not merely submitting a request to COFCO to engage in the business of exporting Japanese kelp. The evidence materials in this case prove that Shengk Dacheng Company was a personal company established by Ma Daqing himself to seize the kelp export business of Shandong Food Company, and Ma Daqing was the actual controller of Shengk Dacheng Company. In September 2006, Ma Daqing established a one-person limited liability company, Shengk Dacheng Company, in the name of his nephew Chen Qingrong (then a student at Qingdao University). Ma Daqing's wife, Yan Suzhen, served as the company's supervisor. Ma Daqing acknowledged that the company's registered capital of 500,000 yuan was provided by himself, and he introduced Shengk Dacheng Company to the Japanese side as his "new company." After Shengk Dacheng Company was established, its only business was exporting kelp to Japan, and Ma Daqing completely operated Shengk Dacheng Company's kelp export business to Japan. The relationship between Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company was obviously not as simple as the relationship between a worker and his former employer. In fact, for such a "Ma's new company" funded, controlled, and introduced by Ma Daqing himself to Japanese customers, the will of Shengk Dacheng Company fully reflected the will of Ma Daqing. There was a common intent between Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company to engage in unfair competition, and they jointly implemented unfair competition acts. Before Ma Daqing left Shanfu Risui Company, he had already jointly implemented unfair competition acts with Shengk Dacheng Company. Therefore, the second-instance court's finding that Shengk Dacheng Company's act of seeking the trading opportunity was merely submitting a request to COFCO to engage in the business of exporting Japanese kelp clearly did not accord with the facts. (3) The second-instance judgment intentionally concealed the time and background of Shandong Food Company's re-obtainment of the 2007 kelp quota. Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company seized the kelp trading opportunities of Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Risui Company, taking away the "livelihood money" of thousands of retired, internal retired, and active employees of Shandong Food Company, provoking strong social repercussions. Employee representatives repeatedly went to the provincial capital and Beijing to petition. Government departments, including the Shandong Provincial Party Committee, the Shandong Provincial Government, the Shandong Provincial Federation of Trade Unions, the Shandong Provincial State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, the Shandong Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, as well as the Ministry of Commerce of the PRC and the China Finance and Trade Union, intervened many times. The Ministry of Commerce and COFCO held multiple meetings for coordination. It was not until July 2007 that Shandong Food Company again obtained 320 tons of the 2007 kelp quota, but by then the kelp harvest season had passed. However, the second-instance judgment concealed this background and found that Shandong Food Company reported its work plan at the request of COFCO and accepted an on-site inspection, and COFCO decided to grant it 320 tons of kelp quota. Shandong Food Company and Shengk Dacheng Company submitted their work plans in January 2007; Shandong Food Company was notified of the loss of the 2007 Weihai area kelp export quota, and Shengk Dacheng Company was notified that it would fully execute the 2007 Weihai area kelp export business to Japan in February 2007; Shandong Food Company was notified of the re-grant of 320 tons of kelp quota in July 2007, completely unrelated to the work plan submission, on-site inspection, etc. 2. Some findings of the second-instance judgment exceeded the claims of the parties. The applicants for retrial never requested the court to find that Ma Daqing had violated a non-compete agreement or that Shengk Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing had infringed trade secrets. However, the second-instance court made findings on whether Ma Daqing had violated a non-compete agreement and whether there was trade secret infringement. These findings substantially deprived the applicants for retrial of the right to sue the respondents for trade secret infringement, causing them to lose the ability to seek protection under other legal provisions when they could not obtain relief in this case. 3. The second-instance judgment incorrectly applied the law. (1) The second-instance judgment's finding that Ma Daqing's conduct was both the legitimate rights and interests of a business operator and consistent with public policy contravened the legislative intent of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. According to the second-instance judgment, as long as there is no statutory or agreed non-compete obligation and no infringement of specific civil rights and interests such as trade secrets, employees can do whatever they want and arbitrarily seize the business opportunities of their former enterprise. This clearly contradicts the basic principles of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Market competition requires fair conditions. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law does not only prohibit the listed types of unfair competition acts; it prohibits all unfair competitive conduct that violates good faith. According to Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, even in the absence of statutory or agreed non-compete obligations and infringement of specific civil rights and interests such as trade secrets, whether before or after resignation, market participants, when engaging in market transactions, must follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith, and abide by generally accepted commercial morality. They cannot engage in unfair competition with their former enterprise by violating the principle of good faith and generally accepted commercial morality. Ma Daqing not only used his position to engage in unfair competition with his former enterprise before leaving, seizing business opportunities that originally belonged to the applicants for retrial, but also continued to engage in unfair competition with the applicants for retrial after leaving by failing to return company business materials, etc., causing huge losses to the applicants for retrial. The second-instance judgment's finding that Ma Daqing did not constitute unfair competition was clearly an incorrect application of the law. (2) The second-instance judgment, based on a one-sided examination of the parties' claims and ignoring the main facts of the case, inevitably led to an incorrect application of the law. In this case, the unfair competition acts of Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company were a series of prepared, step-by-step acts from mid-2006 to after 2007. The second-instance judgment only examined the acts after 2007, ignoring Ma Daqing's acts before his resignation. The greatest difference between the unfair competition acts of Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company and the typified unfair competition acts under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law is that the latter target single, specific acts, and the determination of propriety focuses on the "point" of the actor's conduct. However, the series of acts implemented by Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company were a planned, step-by-step, indivisible whole with strong concealment. Each specific act in this whole may not independently constitute an act expressly prohibited by specific legal norms, but the malice of Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company throughout the entire process of their acts was glaringly obvious. The determination of the propriety of Ma Daqing's and Shengk Dacheng Company's acts must examine the entirety of the conduct. This entirety of conduct, due to the impropriety of its purpose, constituted unfair competition. (3) The second-instance judgment made an obvious restrictive interpretation of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, even equating it directly with violations of non-compete agreements and the express provisions of Chapter 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, without interpreting the Anti-Unfair Competition Law according to generally accepted commercial standards and common understanding, thus incorrectly applying the law. (4) The second-instance judgment confused the relationship between the personal skills of workers and the competitive advantage in the kelp business. The second-instance judgment simply characterized competition in the kelp business as a professional trading opportunity that can be entirely dependent on the personal knowledge and skills of workers, defining personal factors as the sole competitive factor in the kelp business, which clearly seriously deviates from the nature of the kelp export business. (5) The second-instance judgment confused the standards for determining the choice of the counterparty and unfair competition. For unfair competition acts in the field of protection of business opportunities, the standard for determination should be whether the business operator has malice and whether it has implemented unfair competition acts, not the choice of the counterparty. In market competition, the counterparty, for various reasons, may knowingly conduct transactions with an operator whose behavior is improper but still insist on doing so. At this time, because the counterparty has the freedom to choose the transaction object, the law cannot prohibit the counterparty from making such a choice, but the law can prohibit the operator from engaging in the above transaction to maintain a fair competitive order. The second-instance judgment's conclusion that as long as the counterparty recognizes it, there is no unfair competition is erroneous. 4. The second-instance judgment incorrectly allocated the burden of proof, and the civil liability it determined violated legal provisions. Shengk Dacheng Company is a one-person wholly-owned company. When it requested COFCO to engage in the export of kelp to Japan, it had been established for less than three months, had never operated a kelp business, had registered capital of only 500,000 yuan, and had only Ma Daqing as a person engaged in the kelp business. Compared with Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company, the applicants for retrial had obvious competitive advantages in terms of past performance, capital, scale, number of employees, technology, etc. Under normal competitive conditions, the applicants for retrial should have continued to maintain the trading opportunities for exporting kelp to Japan, rather than the drastic change that occurred in this case. Where a result inconsistent with normal competition occurs, the court should presume that Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company engaged in unfair competition and require Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company to prove that the means by which they obtained the kelp export business opportunities were proper. The applicants for retrial requested Ma Daqing and Shengk Dacheng Company to disclose their submitted documents and applied to the court to investigate with COFCO, but the second-instance court ignored this request, which was erroneous. 5. The second-instance judgment ignored the huge investment made by the applicants for retrial in the kelp export business to Japan. The judgment was obviously unfair, caused great harm, and has already had adverse effects.

Respondents Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing jointly responded: The judgment of first instance was unclear in fact, erroneous in characterization of important issues, and incorrect in application of law. The judgment of second instance corrected the errors of the first instance, found clear facts, applied the law correctly, and should be upheld according to law. Meanwhile, Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing further stated: 1. All claims of Shanfu Group Company and Shanfu Rishui Company were dismissed in the judgment of first instance, and they have no substantive rights in the retrial proceedings of this case. 2. In the first instance of this case, the court of first instance, upon the application of Shandong Foodstuffs Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company, ordered the freezing of RMB 6,000,000 in the property of Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company, with an actual freeze of RMB 4,631,669.27. Two days after the judgment of second instance was rendered, Shandong Foodstuffs Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company, based on the same facts, filed a lawsuit for unjust enrichment against Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing, while simultaneously applying for preservation of RMB 6,000,000 in the property of Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company. Through a series of seemingly reasonable litigation-related actions, the retrial applicants dragged Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company into litigation, aiming to exclude other operators, curb competition, and monopolize operations, thereby seriously infringing the interests of Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company, constituting unfair competition. 3. Although Shandong Foodstuffs Company obtained quotas for exporting kelp to Japan in 2007 and 2008 through administrative intervention in the market, the actual quantity of kelp it exported to Japan was far below the quota, and it no longer had the practical capability to maintain a stable quantity and quality of kelp exports to Japan.

The following facts were found in the first instance trial by the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province: Shandong Foodstuffs Company was established on October 26, 1982, with its predecessor being the Shandong Foodstuffs Branch of China National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corporation. On August 1, 2000, Shandong Foodstuffs Company, together with the Employee Shareholding Association of Shandong Shanfude Trading Co., Ltd., Liu Hantao, Li Yuchun, and Li Jie, jointly established Shandong Shanfude Trading Co., Ltd., with Shandong Foodstuffs Company holding 40% of its registered capital. On May 24, 2004, the company applied to change its business name to Shanfu Group Company. On June 16, 2004, Shanfu Group Company contributed capital and jointly established Shanfu Rishui Company with Nippon Suisan Kaisha, Ltd.

Ma Daqing began working at Shandong Foodstuffs Company in 1986 and started engaging in kelp processing and export work in 1988. From August 1, 2000, Ma Daqing signed two labor contracts with Shandong Shanfude Trading Co., Ltd., with the contract period from August 1, 2000, to July 31, 2006. From January 4, 2005, Ma Daqing signed two labor contracts with Shanfu Rishui Company, with the contract period from January 4, 2005, to December 31, 2006. Before the expiration of the contract period, Shanfu Rishui Company notified employees, including Ma Daqing, to negotiate contract renewal before December 1, 2006, stating that failure to do so would be deemed as not renewing the contract with the company, and the labor contract between the parties would automatically terminate. Ma Daqing did not renew the labor contract with Shanfu Rishui Company.

On June 1, 2007, Ma Daqing filed a labor arbitration application with the Qingdao Labor Dispute Arbitration Commission, requesting a ruling that Shanfu Rishui Company handle procedures for termination of the labor contract and transfer of personnel files, and compensate for unemployment insurance benefits of RMB 7,032. Shanfu Rishui Company filed a counterclaim in arbitration, requesting a ruling that Ma Daqing handle the handover of materials, provide a written explanation of the performance of the agreement, and compensate for economic losses of RMB 1,200.

On September 22, 2006, Shengkedacheng Company was established, with the enterprise type being a one-person limited liability company wholly owned by a natural person. The legal representative was Chen Qingrong, with a registered capital of RMB 500,000, and the registered scope of business included aquatic products. Chen Qingrong served as the executive director and manager of the company, subscribing to the entire RMB 500,000 capital contribution; Yan Suzhen served as the supervisor of the company. Yan Suzhen is the spouse of Ma Daqing, and Chen Qingrong is Ma Daqing's nephew. At the time, Chen Qingrong was a student in the 2004 class of the Department of Textile and Garment at Qingdao University. Ma Daqing now works at Shengkedacheng Company.

The Shandong Foodstuffs Branch of China National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corporation (the predecessor of Shandong Foodstuffs Company) began operating kelp export business in 1979. In 1999 and 2000, COFCO Fruit, Vegetable and Aquatic Products Import and Export Company entrusted Shandong Foodstuffs Company to purchase air-dried kelp and handle export procedures on its behalf, with Ma Daqing signing the relevant agreements on behalf of Shandong Foodstuffs Company.

From 2001 to 2006, COFCO Group annually issued "Notices on the Allocation of Export Quantity Quotas for Kelp in [Year]," distributing export quantity quotas for kelp produced in specific regions to Japan among entities including China Food (Beijing) Food Trade Department, COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd., Shandong Foodstuffs Company, Yantai Foodstuffs Import and Export Company, Yantai Kaidi Food Import and Export Co., Ltd., and Dalian Tongsheng Industrial Corporation. Among them, the quantity quotas for kelp produced in the Weihai region exported to Japan obtained by Shandong Foodstuffs Company were: 650 tons each in 2001 and 2002, 620 tons each in 2003 and 2005, and 540 tons in 2006.

After the above quotas were issued, Ma Daqing, primarily on behalf of Shandong Foodstuffs Company or Shanfu Group Company, signed "Sino-Japan Trade Contracts" with companies such as Tokai Suisan Trading Co., Ltd., Mitsui Trading Co., Ltd., and Shinko Trading Co., Ltd., to handle kelp export business. The beneficiaries of the letters of credit stipulated in the contracts were Shandong Foodstuffs Company or Shanfu Group Company.

The "Notices on the Allocation of Export Quantity Quotas for Kelp in [Year]" also consistently stated: Pursuant to the agreement between COFCO Group and the Hokkaido Federation of Fisheries Cooperative Associations of Japan (hereinafter referred to as the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation of Japan), the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation of Japan entrusted COFCO Group to uniformly manage the quotas, quality, and quantity of kelp, and the Japanese side recognized COFCO Group as its sole window for kelp trade in China. For matters related to kelp export trade, companies should contact COFCO Group directly.

From 2000 to 2005, Shandong Foodstuffs Company, Shandong Shanfude Trading Co., Ltd., and Shanfu Group Company signed "Agricultural and Sideline Products Purchase and Sale Contracts" with entities and kelp farming households in the Weihai kelp-producing areas, including the Breeding and Supply Station of Daqin Island Township, Changdao County, and Shandong Mashan Industrial Group Corporation, to purchase air-dried kelp for export to Japan. Ma Daqing signed most of these contracts as an agent.

Shandong Foodstuffs Company is the patentee of the patent for "Kelp Processing Method and Equipment." On September 5, 2006, Ma Daqing once suggested to the company that "there is no need to spend money to renew the kelp patent."

On January 10, 2007, COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. sent a "Notice on Submitting Kelp Business Plans" to Shandong Foodstuffs Company, stating: The change in key personnel originally handling kelp export business at Shandong Foodstuffs Company has attracted the attention of Japanese customers. To ensure the sustained and orderly development of kelp export business, Shandong Foodstuffs Company was required to submit a kelp export work plan before January 17, 2007. COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. would decide on the kelp export operating company based on the actual situation. According to the agreement between COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. and the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation of Japan, the Japanese side entrusted COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. to uniformly manage the quotas, quality, and operating companies for kelp, and the Japanese side recognized the company as its sole window for kelp trade in China.

On the same day, COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. sent a "Notice on Submitting Kelp Business Plans" to Shengkedacheng Company, stating that it had received a fax from Shengkedacheng Company requesting to operate the kelp export business to Japan, and requiring Shengkedacheng Company to submit a kelp export work plan before January 17, 2007.

On January 25, 2007, COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. sent a "Notice on Investigating Kelp Business Plans" to Shandong Foodstuffs Company and Shengkedacheng Company, stating that it would visit the two companies in Qingdao on January 29 to inquire and investigate the relevant contents of the plans.

On February 2, 2007, COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. sent a letter to Shandong Foodstuffs Company, stating that the purpose of this visit was primarily to investigate and understand the 2007 work plan provided by Shandong Foodstuffs Company, and that the 2007 kelp operating quota would be finally decided after discussing the investigation results with the Japanese side.

On February 14, 2007, COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. sent a "Notice on Adjusting the 2007 Kelp Export Operating Rights" to Shandong Foodstuffs Company and Shengkedacheng Company, deciding to transfer the 2007 Weihai kelp export business to Japan to Shengkedacheng Company for execution.

On March 23, 2007, the Shandong Provincial Association of International Economic and Trade sent a letter to the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation of Japan to discuss the allocation of kelp export quotas to Japan. On April 3 of the same year, the Vice President and Representative Director of the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation of Japan, Miyamura Masao, replied: "1. Through Beijing COFCO as the window, we have long had a trade relationship with Shandong Foodstuffs Company; ... 4. Regarding whether Shandong Foodstuffs Company, after the resignation of Mr. Ma and other staff, can guarantee the stable quality and quantity of Weihai kelp, we feel uneasy and have doubts. On the other hand, because Mr. Ma has been engaged in the Weihai kelp business for a long time, possessing rich experience and knowledge, he has been recognized and trusted by the Japanese kelp industry. We have conducted multiple careful consultations with Japanese kelp manufacturers, and based on the materials provided to us by COFCO after listening to and comparing the business plans of both Shandong Foodstuffs Company and Shengkedacheng Company on site, we have determined that, starting from 2007, Shengkedacheng Company is the most suitable company to handle the Weihai kelp business; 5. For us, it is a major premise to ensure the uniform stability of the specified quantity and quality in the kelp trade with China. Therefore, we request that Beijing COFCO designate Mr. Ma's new company (Shengkedacheng Company) as the window enterprise for Weihai kelp."

On April 6, 2007, COFCO Group issued the "Notice on Allocating 2007 Kelp Export Quantity Quotas," and Shengkedacheng Company obtained an export quota of 310 tons of kelp produced in the Weihai region.

On July 5, 2007, Shandong Foodstuffs Company, based on the "Notice on Allocating 2007 Kelp Export Quantity Quotas" issued by COFCO Group, ultimately obtained an export quota of 320 tons of kelp produced in the Weihai region.

On July 30, 2007, Shandong Foodstuffs Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, seeking confirmation that Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing constituted unfair competition, and requesting an order that Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing return all documents and materials related to the kelp business, cease using the three plaintiffs' procurement and export channels to operate the kelp business, compensate the three plaintiffs for operating profit losses of RMB 6,000,000, and reimburse transportation costs, attorney fees, and other actual expenses incurred in handling this case of RMB 100,000.

Upon trial at first instance, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province found that: Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company claimed that the actions of Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing resulted in their loss of trade opportunities for exporting kelp to Japan, thereby constituting unfair competition. They invoked Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law to seek judicial relief from the court. Regardless of whether this claim could be established, the lawsuit constituted a new type of unfair competition dispute, requiring analysis and determination of the following issues:

1. Whether Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law can regulate acts of unfair competition not explicitly provided for therein. Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, as a provision in the General Provisions, is a principle clause. For acts not listed in Chapter 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, regulation should be imposed if the following conditions are met: first, a legitimate operator has obtained a certain competitive advantage through its own efforts; second, another operator has acquired that competitive advantage through improper means and caused losses to the legitimate operator. When an unfair operator commits such an act, the People's Court may regulate such unfair competition in accordance with Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and grant civil judicial relief to the legitimate competitor.

2. Analysis of the nature of the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan. The trade of exporting kelp to Japan operates under the following model: the Japanese government imposes import quota management on kelp from China, with the allocation of these import quotas handled by the Japan Hokkaido Fisheries Federation; the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation entrusts COFCO with unified management of kelp quotas, quality, and quantity; COFCO issues annual notifications informing selected enterprises of the quantities of kelp to be exported to Japan. Enterprises that obtain kelp quantity quotas export kelp to Japanese enterprises in accordance with the allocated quota amounts, while enterprises that do not receive quota allocations cannot export kelp to Japanese enterprises. As can be seen from the reply letter from Masao Miyamura, Vice President of the Japan Hokkaido Fisheries Federation, to the Shandong Provincial International Economic and Trade Federation, the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation plays a leading role in determining which enterprises obtain the quotas for exporting kelp to Japan. From the notifications issued by COFCO over the years regarding kelp export quantity quotas and its 2007 investigation into the kelp export plans of Shandong Food Company and Shengkedacheng Company, COFCO is the direct executing unit for determining the allocation of quotas for domestic enterprises to export kelp to Japan. In short, the so-called "trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan" refers to the qualification obtained by domestic export enterprises through COFCO's allocation to export a specified quantity of kelp from relevant regions to Japan. China adopts a statutory approach to intellectual property protection, meaning that the rights claimed by a party must be explicitly provided for by law. "Trade opportunities for exporting kelp to Japan" are not objects protected by intellectual property law. In essence, they constitute a business opportunity, a position of advantage gained in market competition. In the trade of exporting kelp to Japan, price, quantity, and quality are not the decisive factors for obtaining the transaction opportunity; the key lies in whether one can obtain the qualification to export kelp to Japan. From 2001 onward, this trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan was stably enjoyed by four entities, including Shandong Food Company. These four entities were: the Food Trade Department of China Foods (Beijing) (changed to COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. after 2002, and to COFCO Industrial Food Import and Export Co., Ltd. in 2007), Shandong Food Company, Yantai Food Import and Export Company (changed to Yantai Kaidi Food Import and Export Co., Ltd. after 2002), and Dalian Tongsheng Industrial Corporation (changed to Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. after 2005). The manner in which the four entities obtained the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan was: COFCO allocated to the four entities the purchase and export of kelp in relevant regions through "Notifications on the Issuance of Kelp Export Quantity Quotas for Year XX," with the quantities remaining basically stable over the years. Before 2006, there was no evidence that the above entities obtained kelp export quantity quotas by submitting kelp export plans, nor was there evidence that enterprises other than the four entities could obtain kelp export quantity quotas by submitting kelp export plans. In 2007, there was no evidence that entities other than these four and Shengkedacheng Company could obtain kelp export quantity quotas by submitting kelp export plans. Therefore, this trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan is not one that any enterprise with import and export business qualifications can autonomously obtain from open channels, such as by submitting plans. The ability of these four entities to stably enjoy the trade opportunity for exporting kelp from specific regions to Japan over a long period depended not only on their advantages in operating kelp export businesses within their respective regions but also reflected their good corporate credit in the trade of exporting kelp to Japan. This opportunity to receive a fixed number of kelp export quotas to Japan each year constitutes a favorable condition in competitive relations, through which Shandong Food Company gained a competitive advantage. This competitive advantage acquired by Shandong Food Company was obtained through fair means. It is not that other market operators cannot obtain such a competitive advantage, but if other operators use improper means to obtain it, such conduct is prohibited by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

3. Which party among Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company owned the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan. The three companies jointly asserted that they owned the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan. However, prior to the establishment of Shanfu Group Company, the trade of exporting kelp from the Weihai region to Japan was handled by Shandong Food Company, which held the quotas and actually operated the business. After Shanfu Group Company and Shanfu Rishui Company were successively established, the trade of exporting kelp from the Weihai region to Japan was still carried out under the quotas held by Shandong Food Company, but the actual execution was successively undertaken by these two companies. Before 2007, when COFCO allocated the Weihai region kelp quotas separately to Shandong Food Company and Shengkedacheng Company, COFCO had always allocated the Weihai region kelp quotas to Shandong Food Company and never to Shanfu Group Company or Shanfu Rishui Company. It is thus evident that Shandong Food Company was the holder of the trade opportunity for exporting kelp from the Weihai region to Japan, while the trade opportunities for exporting kelp to Japan enjoyed by Shanfu Group Company and Shanfu Rishui Company both originated from Shandong Food Company. That is, Shandong Food Company obtained the kelp export quotas and then assigned them to Shanfu Group Company and Shanfu Rishui Company for actual execution. Although whether Shandong Food Company could obtain this trade opportunity directly affected the two companies, even so, these two companies were not the direct holders of the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan. Therefore, when a civil dispute arises over the ownership of this trade opportunity, the claims of these two companies, not being the direct holders of the opportunity, should be rejected.

4. Whether Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing engaged in acts of unfair competition. During his employment with Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company, Ma Daqing was always responsible for the purchase and export of kelp to Japan and was familiar with the entire process. In Shengkedacheng Company, where he worked, Chen Qingrong was a relative of Ma Daqing and a college student, and the company's supervisor was Ma Daqing's wife. Neither Shengkedacheng Company nor Ma Daqing proved that the legal representative or supervisor of Shengkedacheng Company had experience in the trade of exporting kelp to Japan or any foreign trade whatsoever. Regarding the business of exporting kelp to Japan, Ma Daqing was the actual operator of Shengkedacheng Company. Shortly after Ma Daqing left Shanfu Rishui Company, Shengkedacheng Company obtained the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan. The legitimacy of this conduct is key to determining whether the actions of Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing constitute unfair competition. First, Shengkedacheng Company directly obtained the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan, which clearly formed direct competition with Shandong Food Company. Second, the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan was not obtained from the market through open and free competition; for many years, Shandong Food Company and three other companies had stably received this export opportunity. The reason Ma Daqing was recognized by the Japan Hokkaido Fisheries Federation was due to the gradual development of his role in handling the export trade of kelp to Japan on behalf of Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company, and not because Japanese customers chose to trade with Shandong Food Company based on their understanding of Ma Daqing's abilities. Even if, as stated by relevant personnel from the Hokkaido Fisheries Federation, Japanese customers fully recognized and only trusted Ma Daqing's business capabilities, Ma Daqing should have recognized that, in the context of the kelp trade opportunity, his actions were only official conduct representing Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company, and were inseparable from the strength and financial support of these companies. As a corporate employee, the competitive advantage formed in the course of performing tasks assigned by the employer, like inventions created in the course of performing work duties, belongs to the company, not the employee. Ma Daqing's appropriation of the competitive advantage belonging to Shandong Food Company for Shengkedacheng Company constituted an abuse of the trust Japanese customers had placed in him based on his performance of official duties, seriously violating the principle of good faith and recognized business ethics. As a legal person, Shengkedacheng Company's operations were actually carried out by Ma Daqing. Therefore, the company knowingly allowed Ma Daqing to act in violation of business ethics, constituting subjective knowledge, and it also violated recognized business ethics. This case does not meet the circumstances of "a customer conducting market transactions with the employing entity based on personal trust in an employee." Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing provided no evidence that Japanese customers chose to trade with Shandong Food Company based on personal trust in Ma Daqing. Although, in form, Shengkedacheng Company obtained the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan by submitting an export plan and after being inspected by relevant units, this method of acquisition cannot be considered legitimate. First, the Japanese side or COFCO did not adopt open competitive methods such as public bidding to select trading partners. The four entities, including Shandong Food Company, had stably obtained the trade opportunity for exporting kelp from their respective regions to Japan over a long period. Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing provided no evidence that enterprises other than Shengkedacheng Company could obtain such opportunities by submitting "kelp business plans." Therefore, it cannot be concluded that Shengkedacheng Company obtained the trade opportunity through fair competition. Regarding whether the unfair competition acts of Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing caused economic losses to Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company: In 2007, Shengkedacheng Company enjoyed a quota of 310 tons for exporting kelp from the Weihai region, whereas previously, the kelp export quotas for the Weihai region were all held by Shandong Food Company. Therefore, it was inevitable that Shandong Food Company suffered losses due to the partial loss of this trade opportunity. Thus, the actions of Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing caused economic losses to Shandong Food Company. In summary, the actions of Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company constituted unfair competition.

5. Regarding the civil liability to be borne by Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing. The actions of Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company constituted unfair competition and caused losses to Shandong Food Company. In accordance with Articles 106, 130, and 134 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, they shall jointly bear the civil liability of ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses on a joint and several basis. Concerning the specific form of ceasing the infringement: To protect the competitive advantage obtained by Shandong Food Company through legitimate transactions, Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company shall not engage in the trade of exporting kelp to Japan in the same manner as Shandong Food Company. However, to protect free competition, once the influence Ma Daqing had on Japanese customers through his performance of official duties gradually disappears, requiring Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing to never engage in the aforementioned trade goes against the basic principle of fair competition. Therefore, a period should be set to eliminate this influence. Considering the circumstances of this case, it is determined that within three years from the date this judgment takes effect, Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing shall not engage in the trade of exporting kelp to Japan in the same manner as Shandong Food Company. Regarding the calculation of the amount of damages: The actual quantity of kelp exported by Shengkedacheng Company was approximately 140 tons. According to statements made by Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing, the value of the kelp was 2.52 million yuan, and after the export of this batch of goods to Japan, the settlement amount was 4,631,669.27 yuan. The difference between the value of the kelp claimed by Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing and the export settlement amount — 2,111,669.27 yuan in profit — should be used as the loss of Shandong Food Company to be compensated. Shandong Food Company's claim for damages exceeding this amount is not supported.

6. Regarding other claims made by Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company. Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company also requested: that Ma Daqing return all documents and materials related to the kelp business; and that Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing cease using the purchase channels of Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company to operate the kelp business. The former involves a labor dispute case currently being heard in another court. In accordance with the principle of res judicata, this claim is not supported. Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company did not provide valid evidence to prove that Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing had used Shandong Food Company's channels to purchase kelp, so this claim is also not supported. On April 10, 2008, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, in accordance with Articles 106, 130, and 134 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered Civil Judgment (2007) Qing Min San Chu Zi No. 136, ruling as follows:
1. Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company shall immediately cease operating the trade of exporting kelp to Japan in the same manner as Shandong Food Company from the date this judgment takes effect, for a period of three years from the date this judgment takes effect.
2. Shengkedacheng Company shall compensate Shandong Food Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 2,111,669.27 yuan.
3. Ma Daqing shall bear joint and several liability for the payment obligation set forth in item 2 above.
4. Shandong Food Company's other claims are rejected.
5. Shanfu Group Company's claims are rejected.
6. Shanfu Rishui Company's claims are rejected.
The case acceptance fee of RMB 54,500 yuan and the property preservation fee of 5,000 yuan shall be borne by Shandong Food Company in the amount of 38,902 yuan, and by Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company jointly in the amount of 20,598 yuan.

Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing, dissatisfied with the above judgment, jointly appealed to the Shandong High People's Court, requesting the reversal of items 1, 2, and 3 of the judgment of first instance and the rejection of all claims made by Shandong Food Company in accordance with the law. Their grounds of appeal were as follows:
1. Some of the facts determined by the court of first instance were erroneous. Shandong Food Company is not currently a shareholder of Shanfu Group Company. Since May 2005, the shareholders of Shanfu Group Company have been four natural persons, Teng Haibo, Wang Fengkai, Liu Hantao, and Wei Shitai, with no legal relationship to Shandong Food Company. Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. was not a successor to Dalian Tongsheng Industrial Company; the two companies are completely independent and unrelated.
2. The judgment of first instance erred in applying Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law to determine that Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing constituted unfair competition. When determining whether a specific act constitutes unfair competition, if there are specific provisions of law that can be referenced and applied, the court should directly apply those specific provisions, and not expand the scope of protection by relying on the principle clause of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing did not constitute any form of unfair competition provided for by any specific provision.
3. The actions of Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing did not constitute unfair competition. The trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan can be obtained through free competition, and the law does not specifically restrict free competition in this industry. Starting in 2005, COFCO cancelled the quota of Dalian Tongsheng Industrial Corporation and transferred it to Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd., which fully demonstrates that the trade opportunity in question was freely allocated by COFCO based on actual circumstances and could be obtained through free competition. Additionally, Shanfu Group Company has no legal connection to Shandong Food Company. The quota for exporting kelp to Japan obtained by Shandong Food Company was entirely transferred to Shanfu Group Company for operation, and the resulting income was also enjoyed by Shanfu Group Company. Shanfu Group Company had effectively obtained the relevant quota from Shandong Food Company, which objectively contradicts the court of first instance's determination that the kelp quotas were stably held by four companies. The process by which COFCO issued the 2007 quotas itself also proves that COFCO has the right to determine the specific allocation of kelp quotas based on the actual competitive situation of enterprises. The trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan cannot be completely monopolized by certain enterprises for historical reasons; other enterprises can fully obtain this business opportunity through free competition. The knowledge and skills learned by an employee in the workplace belong to the employee, who may freely use them unless the law explicitly restricts them. After August 2000, Ma Daqing was no longer an employee of Shandong Food Company. The competitive advantage gained by Ma Daqing through the application of his knowledge and skills no longer belonged to Shandong Food Company. The court of first instance attributed all competitive advantages formed by Ma Daqing in the kelp business to Shandong Food Company, without any legal basis. Even without public bidding, it was still legitimate free competition. The competition regarding kelp quotas in this case does not fall within the scope of matters that must be subject to public tender under the Bidding Law. The court of first instance artificially established that "legitimate free competition" requires the form of "public tender," and this erroneous premise directly led to an erroneous conclusion. The actions of Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing in seeking the kelp quotas did not violate the principle of good faith and recognized business ethics. In this case, when Ma Daqing performed his official duties in 2007, he was acting on behalf of Shengkedacheng Company. Japanese customers were aware of this. Throughout the process, Ma Daqing did not deceive Japanese customers, did not abuse their trust, and did not violate the principle of good faith. Ma Daqing's actions in seeking the kelp quotas did not violate any recognized business ethics. The court of first instance did not elaborate on which recognized business ethics Ma Daqing's actions violated. "An employee cannot engage in the same business as the former employer" cannot become a "recognized business ethics."
4. The court of first instance erred in ordering Shengkedacheng Company and Ma Daqing to pay damages of 2,111,669.27 yuan. The court of first instance did not examine Shengkedacheng Company's costs, and did not deduct various cost items such as expenses for sunshade nets, packaging, and transportation. The actual profit of Shengkedacheng Company is far lower than the amount determined by the court of first instance.

Shandong Food Company responded in its defense: The facts found in the first-instance judgment are clear, the applicable law is correct, and the judgment should be affirmed; the grounds of appeal of Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing have no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed. The reasons are as follows: 1. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly. The first-instance judgment found that Shandong Food Company held 40% of the registered capital of Shanfu Group Company, which refers to the situation at the time of the establishment of Shandong Shanfude Trade Co., Ltd. (later renamed Shanfu Group Company) on August 1, 2000. The formation of the interest pattern whereby Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company jointly enjoyed the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan was due to the historical origin of the succession and flow of personnel and business among Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company, and was not determined by the equity relationship among them; the equity relationship had no substantive impact on the first-instance judgment. That Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. succeeded Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company in obtaining the kelp quota is an objective fact. The "change" referred to in the first-instance judgment here refers to the change in the entity enjoying the trade opportunity for exporting kelp, not the change in the legal person status between Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. and Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company. 2. The first-instance judgment correctly applied the law. What Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company seek to protect is the protectable interest embodied in the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan formed over more than thirty years of operation. Based on this claim, the first-instance judgment's characterization of the case is entirely correct. "A new type of unfair competition dispute" constitutes the nature of the legal relationship in this case and the basis for its trial. Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing, by setting aside the legal relationship claimed by Shandong Food Company and adjudicated by the first-instance court, and arbitrarily establishing other legal relationships, violate basic common sense of civil litigation. Regulating non-typical acts of unfair competition not explicitly provided for by law is the greatest legal value of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Where specialized intellectual property laws do not provide exhaustive protection, the Anti-Unfair Competition Law can certainly be applied for protection. The "trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan" at issue in this case falls within the situation of "not being exhaustively protected by specialized intellectual property laws." The knowledge and skills learned by a worker at the employer are not the same as "the competitive advantage formed by an enterprise employee in the process of performing tasks assigned by the employer." This case does not involve the issue of an individual worker's "knowledge and skills." The "competitive advantage formed by an enterprise employee in the process of performing tasks assigned by the employer" reflects the strength and capital of the relevant enterprise, and also depends on the advantages of the relevant enterprise in operating the kelp export business within the region, as well as its good corporate credit in the trade of exporting kelp to Japan, rather than the knowledge and skills of any individual. The first-instance judgment indeed found that the "trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan" is not an object protected by intellectual property law, but it never stated that it is "not protected by law," which precisely provides the reason and space for protection under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. 3. Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing maliciously seized the business opportunity involved in the case, violating the principles of good faith and recognized commercial ethics, causing huge losses to Shandong Food Company, and constituting unfair competition. Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing employed a series of premeditated improper means to obtain the quota for exporting kelp to Japan from COFCO Group, successfully seizing Shandong Food Company's business opportunity and competitive advantage in exporting kelp to Japan, and attempting to conceal their malice in seizing the business opportunity and competitive advantage through forms such as the so-called "kelp business plan and acceptance of inspection by relevant units."

During the second instance, Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing provided the following new evidence to the Shandong High People's Court: 1. Industrial and commercial registration materials of Shanfu Group from the Shandong Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce, purporting to prove that from May 2005 to the present, Shandong Food Company is not a shareholder of Shanfu Group Company. 2. Industrial and commercial registration materials of Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. and Dalian Tongsheng Industrial Co., Ltd. from the Dalian Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, purporting to prove that there is no relationship between the above two companies. The court of second instance accepted this evidence.

The Shandong High People's Court found upon trial in the second instance that when Shanfu Group Company was established, its name was Shandong Shanfude Trade Co., Ltd., and Shandong Food Company held 40% of its shares. However, from May 2005 to the present, Shandong Food Company is no longer a shareholder of Shanfu Group Company. Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. and Dalian Tongsheng Industrial Co., Ltd. are independent legal persons with no relationship of entity change between them. The first-instance judgment found that from 2001, the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan was stably enjoyed by four units, including Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company, and also found that Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company changed to Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. after 2005, meaning the first-instance judgment actually considered Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. to be the legal entity resulting from the change of Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company. The first-instance judgment was erroneous in this fact finding. Additionally, although the first-instance judgment found that the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan was stably enjoyed by four units from 2001, it actually listed eight units nominally enjoying the trade opportunity without ascertaining the relationship among these eight nominal units. Therefore, the first-instance judgment's finding on this fact is inconsistent. Other facts are consistent with those found by the first-instance court.

The Shandong High People's Court held in its second-instance trial that the focus of the dispute between the parties is whether the actions of Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing constitute unfair competition under Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. The trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan involved in this case is the qualification obtained by a domestic enterprise to export a specific quantity of kelp from a relevant region to Japan, which is a transaction opportunity. In 2007, Shengke Dacheng Company obtained this transaction opportunity, and Shandong Food Company's kelp export quota correspondingly decreased, causing harm to Shandong Food Company from Shengke Dacheng Company's acquisition of the transaction opportunity. However, competition itself is an act by operators to compete with each other for transaction opportunities; in the gain or loss of transaction opportunities, harm is often caused to competitors. Although such harm is a necessary condition for constituting unfair competition, it is not a sufficient condition. Merely causing harm does not necessarily constitute unfair competition; whether it constitutes unfair competition must also be determined by whether the relevant competitive conduct is improper. The determination of impropriety is mainly based on the principles set forth in Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. To this end, it is necessary to determine from the following two aspects: 1. Whether Ma Daqing and Shengke Dacheng Company's actions in obtaining the trade opportunity were improper. Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Operators in market transactions shall follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, good faith, and abide by recognized commercial ethics. Unfair competition as referred to in this Law means acts that violate the provisions of this Law, harm the lawful rights and interests of other operators, and disrupt the social and economic order. Operators as referred to in this Law mean legal persons, other economic organizations, and individuals engaged in commodity trading or profit-making services (hereinafter commodities include services)." This article is a principle provision, clarifying the scope of unfair competition acts regulated by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law — it regulates acts that violate the provisions of this Law in market transactions and harm the lawful rights and interests of other operators. Shandong Food Company filed a lawsuit with the first-instance court, seeking relief under this provision for its trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan. From the facts found in this case, in 2007, Shengke Dacheng Company applied to COFCO Group to engage in the kelp trade, then reported a work plan at COFCO Group's request, accepted an on-site inspection by COFCO Group, and ultimately the Japan Hokkaido Fisheries Federation decided to grant it a quantity quota of 310 tons of kelp for export to Japan. During this period, Shandong Food Company also reported a work plan at COFCO Group's request and accepted an on-site inspection, and COFCO Group decided to grant it a quantity quota of 320 tons. In the alleged infringing conduct, Ma Daqing, on behalf of Shengke Dacheng Company, requested COFCO Group to engage in the trade of exporting kelp to Japan and obtained a quantity quota for exporting kelp to Japan. Therefore, it is necessary to first analyze whether Ma Daqing's conduct was improper. Starting in 1986, Ma Daqing successively worked at Shandong Food Company, Shandong Shanfu Food Import and Export Co., Ltd., Shandong Shanfude Trade Co., Ltd., and Shanfu Rishui Company. When representing Shengke Dacheng Company in seeking the trade opportunity from COFCO Group, Ma Daqing had already left Shandong Food Company, and his contract with Shanfu Rishui Company had also expired and terminated. On April 3, 2007, Miyamura Masao, Vice Chairman of the Representative Committee of the Japan Hokkaido Fisheries Federation, replied in a letter: "Because Mr. Ma (Ma Daqing) has been engaged in the Weihai kelp business for a long time and has rich experience and knowledge, he has been recognized and trusted by the Japanese kelp industry. After repeated and careful consultations with Japanese domestic manufacturers, and based on the information provided by COFCO Group after listening to and comparing the business plans of the two companies locally, we have determined that, from 2007, Shengke Dacheng Company is the most suitable company for the Weihai kelp business. We request that COFCO Group designate Shengke Dacheng Company as the window company for Weihai kelp." It can be seen that when Ma Daqing was seeking to engage in the business of exporting kelp to Japan for Shengke Dacheng Company, he clearly stated that he was representing Shengke Dacheng Company and did not use the name of Shandong Food Company. COFCO Group and the Japan Hokkaido Fisheries Federation knew that Ma Daqing had left Shandong Food Company and, based on their trust in Ma Daqing personally, granted Shengke Dacheng Company the trade opportunity involved in the case. Therefore, after leaving Shandong Food Company, Ma Daqing helped Shengke Dacheng Company obtain the trade opportunity in a proper manner, without violating the principle of good faith, and his conduct was not improper; it constituted fair competition. Regarding whether Shengke Dacheng Company's conduct was improper, its actions in seeking the trade opportunity were merely requesting COFCO Group to engage in the business of exporting kelp to Japan. The allocation of the above quota was the result of COFCO Group and the Japan Hokkaido Fisheries Federation comprehensively assessing the capabilities of both parties. In the competitive process, Shengke Dacheng Company did not violate recognized commercial ethics or the principle of good faith, and its conduct was not improper. Therefore, Ma Daqing's conduct in helping Shengke Dacheng Company seek the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan after lawfully leaving Shandong Food Company and other enterprises was not improper, and Shandong Food Company cannot obtain relief under Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. 2. Whether finding that Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing's conduct does not constitute unfair competition is consistent with the legislative purpose of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. In a market economy, operators enjoy the freedom to compete, and only in exceptional circumstances is it necessary to prohibit unfair competition. Article 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "This Law is enacted to safeguard the healthy development of the socialist market economy, encourage and protect fair competition, prohibit unfair competition acts, and protect the lawful rights and interests of operators and consumers." Free and fair competition is a necessary condition for the healthy development of the socialist market economy. Safeguarding the healthy development of the market economy and encouraging and protecting fair competition are among the legislative purposes of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Therefore, when applying the law, it is necessary to balance the encouragement and protection of fair competition with the prevention and restriction of unfair competition. From the legislative structure, Articles 5 to 15 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law list eleven specific types of unfair competition acts. For operators whose lawful rights and interests are harmed by the above eleven types of unfair competition, they may seek protection under the provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. For competitive acts not specifically provided for by law, only when they can be determined to violate the principle provisions of the law based on recognized commercial standards and common understanding under the market economy environment can they be found to constitute unfair competition under Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. When determining whether a specific act constitutes unfair competition, the legislative purpose of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law must not be violated or deviated from, and the scope of unfair competition must not be improperly expanded so as to hinder free and fair competition. Specifically in this case, there is no non-competition agreement between Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Rishui Company, and Ma Daqing restricting Ma Daqing from engaging in competitive business after leaving. Ma Daqing has the freedom to choose his occupation after leaving. Even if he uses the experience in the trade of exporting kelp to Japan accumulated during his employment to engage in competitive business after leaving, Shandong Food Company and Shanfu Rishui Company have no right to prohibit it. Shandong Food Company or Shanfu Rishui Company did not treat the trade opportunity for exporting kelp to Japan as their trade secret, nor did they agree with Ma Daqing to keep it as a trade secret. Ma Daqing's acquisition of the trade opportunity does not involve infringement of their trade secrets. Moreover, in this case, Shandong Food Company did not seek judicial protection under the specific provisions on non-competition agreements or trade secret infringement. In the absence of statutory or agreed non-competition obligations and without infringement of specific civil rights such as trade secrets, this is both a lawful right of the operator and consistent with public policy. Therefore, the first-instance judgment's finding that Ma Daqing's conduct seriously violated the principle of good faith and recognized commercial ethics, constituting unfair competition, was improper. In summary, Ma Daqing's alleged conduct did not violate the principle of good faith or recognized commercial ethics; his conduct was not improper and did not constitute unfair competition. There was no agreement between Shandong Food Company and Ma Daqing to keep trade secrets, nor statutory or agreed non-competition obligations. Shandong Food Company cannot restrict Ma Daqing's free competition or obtain special protection under Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. The first-instance judgment's protection of the conduct involved under Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law constituted an error in the application of law. The first-instance judgment's order that Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing immediately cease operating the trade of exporting kelp to Japan in the same manner as Shandong Food Company, with the prohibition lasting for three years from the effective date of the judgment, effectively imposed a statutory non-competition obligation on Ma Daqing, which has no legal basis. Shandong Food Company's claim against Shengke Dacheng Company was based on whether Ma Daqing's above conduct was improper. Given that Ma Daqing's conduct did not constitute unfair competition, Shengke Dacheng Company's impropriety cannot be established either. Moreover, Shengke Dacheng Company has no statutory or agreed non-competition obligations, has not infringed any specific lawful rights and interests, and does not constitute unfair competition. Other alleged unfair competition acts by Shandong Food Company were either not supported by valid evidence or were being tried in separate cases, and its claims are not supported. In conclusion, the appeal grounds of Shengke Dacheng Company and Ma Daqing are established, and their appeal requests should be supported. The first-instance judgment erred in part in its factual findings, improperly applied the law, and reached an incorrect conclusion, and should be reversed. After deliberation by the Judicial Committee of the Shandong High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: 1. The civil judgment (2007) Qing Min San Chu Zi No. 136 of the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province is reversed; 2. The claims of Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company are dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 54,500, the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 23,693 shall be borne by Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company.

This Court finds upon examination that the facts found by the court of second instance are essentially accurate. It is further found that: Since 2001, COFCO Group has annually issued a "Notice on the Allocation of Export Quotas for Kelp in XX Year" to allocate export quotas for kelp from specific regions to Japan to relevant units. In 2001, the quotas were obtained by four units: Shandong Food Company, Yantai Food Import and Export Company, Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company, and China Food (Beijing) Food Trade Department; in 2002 and 2003, the quotas were obtained by four units: Shandong Food Company, Yantai Kaidi Food Import and Export Co., Ltd., Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company, and COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; in 2005 and 2006, the quotas were obtained by four units: Shandong Food Company, Yantai Kaidi Food Import and Export Co., Ltd., Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd., and COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. After Dalian Guanyu Food Co., Ltd. obtained the Dalian region's export quota for kelp to Japan in 2005, Dalian Tongsheng Industrial General Company did not obtain the quota thereafter.

On February 14, 2007, COFCO International (Beijing) Co., Ltd. issued a notice to Shandong Food Company titled "Notice on Adjusting the 2007 Kelp Export Operation Rights," stating: "On January 30, we sent personnel to Qingdao specifically to investigate and understand the relevant specific issues. After that, we communicated and studied the relevant situation with Japanese customers on multiple occasions. Considering various factors and after seeking the opinion of the Japanese side, we hereby formally notify your company: from 2007, the business of exporting Weihai kelp to Japan will no longer be handled by your company." Subsequently, relevant domestic government departments and industry organizations expressed concern over Shandong Food Company's kelp export quota to Japan. On February 14, 2007, the Shandong Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation sent a letter to the Economic and Commercial Counselor's Office of the Chinese Embassy in Japan, requesting that office reflect the issue of Shandong Food Company's export quota for kelp to Japan to the Japan Fisheries Agency and relevant institutions. On March 1, 2007, the Shandong Provincial State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission sent a letter to the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council (SASAC), requesting that SASAC coordinate with "COFCO Company" to properly handle the issue of the export quota for dried kelp to Japan.

On September 5, 2006, Ma Daqing signed a document regarding a kelp patent bearing the stamp of "Aquatic Products Department II," in which it was mentioned that "there is no need to spend money to renew the kelp patent." Shandong Food Company stated clearly during the hearing before this Court that the patent is a patent for "Kelp Processing Method and Equipment," which remains valid.

During the first instance proceedings, to prove that Ma Daqing and Shengkedacheng Company had engaged in unfair competition practices, Shandong Food Company, Shanfu Group Company, and Shanfu Rishui Company submitted the following evidence: results of the inquiry into private enterprise registration information from Qingdao Administration for Industry and Commerce; documents on the supervisors, directors, and managers of Shengkedacheng Company; the company registration review form; the company registration application; the list of shareholders (incorporators) of the company; two cash payment slips from Agricultural Bank of China; Ma Daqing's Employee Resume; information from the Qingdao Population Inquiry System on current permanent residents; a certificate issued by Qingdao University; the "Minutes of Meeting between Shandong Food Import and Export Company Chairman Teng Haibo and Hokkaido Fisheries Federation Chairman Miyamura, et al."; notarized testimony of seven witnesses including Han Jifeng, Yu Sijin, Zhang Yongli, Deng Zhong'en, Shao Cong, Zhang Zongcheng, and Sun Bingwei; and also applied for witnesses Liu Bing and Liu Hong to testify in court. Shengkedacheng Company submitted notarized testimony of five persons including Han Jifeng, Yu Sijin, Zhang Yongli, Shao Cong, and Sun Bingwei, as well as other evidence as rebuttal evidence.
